chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from 'Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who is permitted to marry a woman with whom he has been committing fornication. He said: If he perceives maturity (or good conduct) in her, then yes (it is permissible). Otherwise, he should court her for fornication. If she continues with him, she becomes forbidden to him. And if she refuses, he should marry her.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying a woman one has been committing fornication with according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Istibsar addresses the transition from illicit relations (zina) to marriage, emphasizing the Imam's pragmatic approach to verifying the woman's commitment to ending the fornication. The condition of 'rushd' (maturity/good conduct) serves as a preliminary indicator of her suitability, while the subsequent test of refusing further fornication confirms her readiness for a lawful union, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of removing the barrier of 'fajr' through mutual consent and cessation of the act.
